scope: All 111 current source identities in the length register, preserving current, branch, family and system distinctions.
rules: Retain upper boundary depth, lower boundary depth, vertical thickness, maximum-speed core depth and reported vertical extent as distinct metrics. A core depth or deepest reported reach does not establish thickness.

Use metres below the local sea surface, positive downward, only where the source reports depths in metres. Preserve pressure in dbar separately; no pressure-to-depth conversion without latitude, method and uncertainty.
Every reference needs an exact current identity, geographic support, source locator, source definition and temporal scope. A regional reference is not a whole-route depth.
Retain source synthesis, observed section, model-derived estimate and projected scenario as distinct evidence kinds. Source summaries do not become independently repeated observations.

Numeric bounds are not automatically uncertainty bounds. Preserve approximation, source variability ranges, standard deviations and measurement uncertainty separately. Never invent percentage margins.
Season labels do not imply fixed calendar months or a sampled annual minimum/maximum. Sparse seasonal descriptions do not support interpolated monthly playback.
Missing values remain null. Do not infer zero-depth upper boundaries, seabed lower boundaries, full-water-column occupation or uniform along-route thickness.
Family or system references do not fill their individual members, and individual branch measurements do not establish the full family or system.

Volume requires compatible horizontal and vertical geometry, identity, time and boundary definitions. Do not multiply unrelated length, width and depth extrema or convert transport in Sv into stored volume.
The initial register contains scoped depth references only. No reference is admitted to physical volume, state intersections, annual extrema or seasonal animation by this collection step.
A reported core-depth range describes where the core occurs, not its vertical thickness. A reported saline-flow band does not define paired whole-current boundaries.
Retain strict reach bounds as strict bounds with no invented point or finite upper endpoint.

Core thickness is the maximum vertical extent of the source-defined threshold core at a longitude, not automatically the thickness at every lateral point. Separate longitude-specific extrema and across-longitude statistics from seasonal variability and uncertainty.
Explicit source months may be retained with a calendar locator; never infer month membership from a season label alone.
Freeze previous source facts and registers. Preserve the entire preceding evidence list before appending qualified references.

The source-selected vertical domain of an inverse-model transport section is a distinct depth metric. Retain its station/layer selection and reported depth cells; density surfaces need not have uniform metre depths across the section.
A section-sampling window dates the entire section, not the selected boundary stations. An inverse-model decade group is not a decade mean, annual envelope or repeated monthly sampling.
A common source row may link width and depth extents, but their product is not cross-sectional area without the vertical and lateral shape. No rectangle or volume is inferred.

Retain a source strict upper bound as upper_bound_m with upper_bound_exclusive=true. This is a one-sided bound on the numeric depth metric, not the upper flow boundary; do not convert it to a point, a zero-to-bound thickness, a confidence interval or an annual maximum.
Retain overlapping observation records as overlapping cases. Different averaging methods, spatial sections or periods do not establish independent repeats or a temporal/error range.

A source statement that flow continues below its sampling limit may support a strict lower bound on reported reach; the sampling limit itself does not become a detected flow boundary. Model and observational extents remain separately qualified.
